comments.note: DapperTagsRepository.CreateTagAsync passes C# bool Highlight as a numeric (0/1) Dapper parameter, but the `highlight` column is ENUM('yes','no'). Inserting Highlight=false sends ordinal 0 (empty string) which causes DATA TRUNCATED in strict mode. Inserting Highlight=true sends ordinal 1 ('yes') which works. Read path in GetAllTagsAsync also fails: Dapper cannot parse 'no' as bool. Fix: either add a Dapper TypeHandler<bool> that converts yes/no, or change the column to TINYINT(1), or use a string intermediate in TagRow. This blocks any test (or production scenario) that creates a tag with Highlight=false.

DapperTagsRepository.DeleteTagAsync performs 5 DELETE/UPDATE steps without wrapping them in a database transaction. A partial failure (e.g., process crash between step 2 and step 3) would leave orphaned tags_movies or tags_grants rows. Fix: wrap the cascade in a transaction using the existing connection.

AddGrantAsync in DapperTagsRepository has no cycle guard — it is the caller's (TagsManager) responsibility to check WouldCreateGrantCycle first. This implicit contract is not documented on the interface or method. A code comment on ITagsRepository.AddGrantAsync noting that cycle detection is the caller's responsibility would prevent misuse.

comments.note: BLOCKING BUG — DapperTagsRepository.TagRow.Highlight is declared as 'bool Highlight'. The 'highlight' column is ENUM('yes','no'), identical in kind to 'review' which is handled via string-intermediate in DapperMovieRepository. Sending a C# bool to an ENUM column via Dapper: (a) bool false → ordinal 0 → empty string → DATA TRUNCATED or silent corruption in strict/non-strict mode respectively; (b) GetAllTagsAsync reads back 'no'/'yes' strings as bool, which Dapper cannot parse, silently returning false for all rows. FIX: change TagRow.Highlight to 'string Highlight { get; set; } = "no";', change ToTag mapping to 'Highlight = string.Equals(r.Highlight, "yes", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)', and change CreateTagAsync/UpdateTagAsync to pass 'highlight: tag.Highlight ? "yes" : "no"' as the Dapper parameter. This is the established project pattern documented in constraints.md and implemented in DapperMovieRepository.cs.

BLOCKING BUG — DapperTagsRepository.DeleteTagAsync performs 5 DB operations (steps 2-5: DELETE tags_movies, DELETE tags_grants, UPDATE parent, DELETE tag) without a wrapping database transaction. A process crash or DB error between any two steps leaves orphaned tags_movies/tags_grants rows or an inconsistent parent pointer. FIX: obtain a transaction from the connection via BeginTransactionAsync() and pass it to all ExecuteAsync calls in steps 2-5. Pattern is already in the codebase: see DapperTagsRepositoryTests.cs constructor (SharedConnectionFactory wraps a shared transaction), and DeleteCategoryAsync (though that is only a 2-step guarded delete). Wrap steps 1-5 in a transaction that commits only when step 5 succeeds.

comments.note: REGRESSION in BUG 2 fix — DapperTagsRepository.DeleteTagAsync (src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/DapperTagsRepository.cs ~line 205) calls connection.BeginTransaction() unconditionally. In production with a fresh connection this is correct. But the test SharedTransactionalConnectionFactory (tests/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests/TestHelpers/SharedTransactionalConnectionFactory.cs) wraps a single MySqlConnection with an already-active IDbTransaction for shared-rollback cleanup. When DeleteTagAsync calls connection.BeginTransaction(), NonDisposingConnection.BeginTransaction() delegates to _inner.BeginTransaction() on the real MySqlConnection which already has an active transaction, causing: System.InvalidOperationException: Transactions may not be nested. Test DeleteTag_CascadesAssociationsAndReparentsChildren FAILS.

FIX RECOMMENDATION for the nested-transaction regression: Two options. OPTION A (production code fix — preferred): In DeleteTagAsync, use a try/catch on BeginTransaction() to detect an already-active transaction and fall through with null transaction parameter; NonDisposingConnection.CreateCommand() will still auto-enlist all commands in the ambient test transaction, and in production only a real nested-transaction error would reach this catch. Pattern: IDbTransaction? ownedTx = null; bool ownsTx = false; try { ownedTx = connection.BeginTransaction(); ownsTx = true; } catch (InvalidOperationException) { /* ambient transaction active */ } ... ExecuteAsync(..., ownedTx) ... if (ownsTx) ownedTx?.Commit(); catch { if (ownsTx) ownedTx?.Rollback(); throw; } OPTION B (test infrastructure fix): Modify NonDisposingConnection.BeginTransaction() to return a no-op wrapper around _transaction when _transaction is non-null, so BeginTransaction() does not delegate to _inner. The no-op wrapper must have Commit()/Rollback() that are no-ops (outer test transaction manages lifecycle). Option A is preferred because it makes production code resilient to ambient transactions without changing test infrastructure.
